newsitem.title: INDIA: India puts tax on consulting engineers, job firms.
newsitem.headline: India puts tax on consulting engineers, job firms.

text.p: The Indian Finance Ministry said on Wednesday that a five percent service tax on consulting engineers and manpower recruitment agencies will take effect on July 7.
A ministry spokeswoman said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had indicated when he unveiled the 1997/98 (April-March) budget in February that a service tax would be levied on the two sectors.
But neither the level of the tax nor the effective date had been announced, she said.
The ministry said in a statement that the service tax would apply to engineering firms including partnership firms, private limited companies, public limited companies and similar establishments.

The tax, which will also cover professionally qualified engineers doing consultancy work, will be computed at five percent of the gross amount which the consulting engineer or engineering firm charges the client.
But expenses incurred by the engineer or the engineering firm which are reimbursed by the client on actuals basis will not be included.
It said the service tax will not apply to consultancy provided to projects based abroad, provided the consultancy charges are received in convertible foreign currency.
As for manpower recruitment agencies, the tax will fall on all commercial concerns engaged in providing any service, directly or indirectly, for recruitment of manpower to a client.
The tax will be computed at five percent of the gross amount charged by the agency from the client in relation to the recruitment of manpower.
